trigger.summary: The frozen hard constraint invalid_rate <= 0 is unsatisfiable across the main matrix, independently of the optimizer.

evidence.probe_n: gsm8k invalid 0/246, Wilson 95% CI (0, 0.0154); the observed 1-in-24 is consistent with that bound (P(>=1 in 24) = 0.311)
evidence.matrix_arithmetic: 40 units x 24 holdout samples; at a true rate of 0.01, P(all 40 units pass) = 0.0001 under the frozen constraint

amendment.rationale: Invalidity is a reported metric, not a stopping rule. A zero-tolerance per-unit gate converts an expected rare event into total experiment failure; it stopped the 2026-08-24 run for a reason unrelated to the optimizer. The retained gate exists only to catch a genuinely broken extractor.

threshold_selection.method: chosen so that false stops are negligible at measured rates while a broken extractor is still detected

accuracy_denominator.decision: invalid samples are counted as INCORRECT and remain in the denominator
accuracy_denominator.rationale: Excluding invalid samples would let an optimizer raise measured accuracy by driving hard questions to invalid output. Keeping them in the denominator makes that strategy strictly self-defeating.
accuracy_denominator.behaviour_change: none; this documents and pins the existing semantics
